blocks.p: **{{لِأَنَّ}} “because”** is followed by a noun ending in -a, or by an ending: {{لِأَنَّ الْجَوَّ جَمِيلٌ}} “because the weather is nice”, {{لِأَنَّهُ مَشْغُولٌ}} “because he's busy”, {{لِأَنِّي|li-annī}} “because I…”. A later lesson shows the whole family of words that work like it.
**{{لِـ}} “in order to”** is followed by the -a form, like {{أَنْ}}: {{جِئْتُ لِأَتَعَلَّمَ}} “I came (in order) to learn”.

ex.t: يُمْكِنُكَ أَنْ تَأْتِيَ الْيَوْمَ أَوْ غَدًا.
ex.r: yumkinuka an taʾtiya l-yawma aw ghadan.
ex.tr: You can come today or tomorrow.
I don't drink coffee because it makes me tired.

ex.t: كَانَ الْجَوُّ حَارًّا، لِذَلِكَ بَقِينَا فِي الْبَيْتِ.
ex.r: kāna l-jawwu ḥārran, li-dhālika baqīnā fī l-bayti.
ex.tr: It was hot, so we stayed home.
I went to the market to buy bread.

blocks.tip: {{أَمْ}} is for choices in questions (“tea or coffee?”); {{أَوْ}} for everything else.

mistakes.why: After {{لِأَنَّ}}, the noun takes -a.
A pronoun after {{لِأَنَّ}} is an ending: li-annahu.

practice.tr: I went to the market to buy bread.

practice.q: A man says “I stayed home because I was tired.”
practice.answer: بَقِيتُ فِي الْبَيْتِ لِأَنِّي كُنْتُ مُتْعَبًا.
practice.r: baqītu fī l-bayti li-annī kuntu mutʿaban.

practice.q: Your turn: say why you're learning Arabic, and one thing you'd like to do but can't, and why.

answers.tr: I'm learning Arabic because I love travelling.

answers.t: أُرِيدُ أَنْ أُسَافِرَ، لَكِنْ لَيْسَ عِنْدِي وَقْتٌ.
answers.r: urīdu an usāfira, lākin laysa ʿindī waqtun.
answers.tr: I'd like to travel, but I don't have time.

lessons.title: Say when things happen
lessons.summary: “When I arrived, he was asleep”, “before you leave”, “after the film”, “for two years”.

goal.tr: When I arrived, everyone was asleep.

dialog.tr: How long have you been learning Arabic?

dialog.t: مُنْذُ سَنَةٍ. بَدَأْتُ عِنْدَمَا انْتَقَلْتُ إِلَى عَمَّانَ.
dialog.r: mundhu sanatin. badaʾtu ʿindamā ntaqaltu ilā ʿammāna.
dialog.tr: For a year. I started when I moved to Amman.

dialog.t: وَهَلْ تَدْرُسُ قَبْلَ الْعَمَلِ أَمْ بَعْدَهُ؟
dialog.r: wa-hal tadrusu qabla l-ʿamali am baʿdahu?
dialog.tr: And do you study before work or after it?

dialog.t: بَعْدَ أَنْ أَرْجِعَ إِلَى الْبَيْتِ، كُلَّ مَسَاءٍ.
dialog.r: baʿda an arjiʿa ilā l-bayti, kulla masāʾin.
dialog.tr: After I get home, every evening.

table: {{قَبْلَ أَنْ تَخْرُجَ|qabla an takhruja}} before you go out
{{بَعْدَ أَنْ أَكَلْنَا|baʿda an akalnā}} after we ate
{{بَيْنَمَا كُنْتُ أَطْبُخُ|baynamā kuntu aṭbukhu}} while I was cooking

blocks.p: {{قَبْلَ أَنْ}} takes the -a form ({{قَبْلَ أَنْ تَنَامَ}} “before you sleep”); {{بَعْدَ أَنْ}} the past for what happened ({{بَعْدَ أَنْ وَصَلْنَا}}) and the -a form for what usually happens ({{بَعْدَ أَنْ أَرْجِعَ}}).

**{{مُنْذُ}} with the present** says how long something has been going on: {{أَسْكُنُ هُنَا مُنْذُ خَمْسِ سَنَوَاتٍ.|askunu hunā mundhu khamsi sanawātin.}} “I've been living here for five years.” English says “have been”; Arabic just uses the present.

ex.tr: After work we go to the café.
I've been learning Arabic for a year.
I waited for him until the evening.
While I was cooking, the phone rang.

blocks.tip: {{مَتَى}} asks “when?”; {{عِنْدَمَا}} says “when…” inside a sentence: {{مَتَى تَصِلُ؟}} “When do you arrive?”, {{عِنْدَمَا أَصِلُ}} “when I arrive”.

mistakes.tr: When I arrived, he was asleep.
mistakes.why: {{مَتَى}} only asks questions; in a sentence, “when” is {{عِنْدَمَا}}.
Before a verb: {{قَبْلَ أَنْ}} and the -a form.

practice.tr: When I arrived, everyone was asleep.

options: I lived here two years ago.
I've been living here for two years.
I'll live here for two years.

practice.tr: After work we go to the café.

practice.q: Tell a man: “Call me before you come.”
Your turn: say how long you've been doing something, and what you do after work or school.

answers.t: أَسْكُنُ فِي هَذِهِ الْمَدِينَةِ مُنْذُ ثَلَاثِ سَنَوَاتٍ.
answers.r: askunu fī hādhihi l-madīnati mundhu thalāthi sanawātin.
answers.tr: I've been living in this city for three years.
After work I walk in the park.

lessons.title: Say what you think, and what people said
lessons.summary: “I think he's busy”, “She said she was tired”, “The house is small, but the garden is big”.
lessons.topic: {{أَنَّ}} “that”, {{إِنَّ}} after {{قَالَ}}, and their family ({{لَكِنَّ}}, {{لِأَنَّ}}, {{لَعَلَّ}}): the noun after them takes -a

goal.tr: I think the restaurant is closed today.
goal.note: -un links to the next word with an i: mughlaquni l-yawma

dialog.t: أَيْنَ سَامِي؟ لَمْ يَرُدَّ عَلَى الْهَاتِفِ.
dialog.r: ayna sāmī? lam yarudda ʿalā l-hātifi.
dialog.tr: Where's Sami? He didn't answer the phone.
I think he's in a meeting.
But he said he'd call me!

blocks.p: To say “that” before a whole sentence (“I think that…”), Arabic uses {{أَنَّ|anna}}. The noun right after it ends in -a, and a pronoun joins it as an ending: {{أَعْرِفُ أَنَّ الْمَتْحَفَ مُغْلَقٌ.|aʿrifu anna l-matḥafa mughlaqun.}} “I know (that) the museum is closed.”, {{أَظُنُّ أَنَّهُ مَشْغُولٌ.|aẓunnu annahu mashghūlun.}} “I think he's busy.”

After {{قَالَ}} “to say”, the word is {{إِنَّ|inna}}: {{قَالَ إِنَّهُ سَيَأْتِي.|qāla innahu sa-yaʾtī.}} “He said he would come.” The same family, all followed by -a: {{لِأَنَّ}} “because” (you met it), {{لَكِنَّ|lākinna}} “but” (before a noun or an ending), {{كَأَنَّ|ka-anna}} “as if”, {{لَعَلَّ|laʿalla}} “perhaps, hopefully”.
Don't mix it up with {{أَنْ}} (an), which comes before a **verb**: {{أُرِيدُ أَنْ أَذْهَبَ}}. {{أَنَّ}} (anna, with a shadda) comes before a **noun or a pronoun ending**.

ex.tr: It looks like the weather will be nice.
The house is small, but the garden is big.

blocks.tip: {{إِنَّ}} can also start a sentence just to stress it, as in speeches and the news: {{إِنَّ الْوَضْعَ صَعْبٌ.|inna l-waḍʿa ṣaʿbun.}} “The situation is (indeed) difficult.”

mistakes.tr: I know that the museum is closed.
mistakes.why: After {{أَنَّ}}, the noun takes -a.
A pronoun after {{أَنَّ}} is an ending: annahu.

practice.tr: The house is small, but the garden is big.

practice.q: Your turn: give your opinion about your city or your job with {{أَظُنُّ أَنَّ…}}, and report something a friend said.

answers.tr: I think my city is very beautiful.
My friend said the film is great.

lessons.title: Make plans with “if”
lessons.summary: “If the weather's nice, we'll go to the sea”, “If you need anything, call me”, “If I were you…”.
lessons.topic: {{إِذَا}} + past for real conditions (with {{فَـ}}); {{لَوْ}} … {{لَـ}} for imagined ones

goal.t: إِذَا كَانَ الْجَوُّ جَمِيلًا، فَسَنَذْهَبُ إِلَى الْبَحْرِ.
goal.r: idhā kāna l-jawwu jamīlan, fa-sa-nadhhabu ilā l-baḥri.
goal.tr: If the weather's nice, we'll go to the sea.

dialog.t: إِذَا انْتَهَيْتُ مِنَ الْعَمَلِ مُبَكِّرًا، فَسَآتِي.
dialog.r: idhā ntahaytu mina l-ʿamali mubakkiran, fa-sa-ātī.
dialog.tr: If I finish work early, I'll come.
And if you're late, call me.

blocks.p: **A real possibility**: {{إِذَا|idhā}} + the **past**, even when you mean now or later: {{إِذَا انْتَهَيْتُ مُبَكِّرًا}} “if I finish early” (word for word: if I finished).

If the second half starts with {{سَـ}}, a command, {{لَا}}, or a sentence without a verb, put {{فَـ}} in front of it: {{إِذَا تَأَخَّرْتَ، فَاتَّصِلْ بِي.}} “If you're late, call me.”, {{إِذَا كَانَ الْجَوُّ جَمِيلًا، فَسَنَذْهَبُ.}}

**Something imagined, not real**: {{لَوْ|law}} + past, and {{لَـ}} on the result: {{لَوْ كُنْتُ غَنِيًّا، لَسَافَرْتُ حَوْلَ الْعَالَمِ.|law kuntu ghaniyyan, la-sāfartu ḥawla l-ʿālami.}} “If I were rich, I'd travel around the world.” It also covers the past: {{لَوْ عَرَفْتُ، لَأَخْبَرْتُكَ.}} “If I'd known, I'd have told you.”
{{إِنْ|in}} is a formal “if”, best known from {{إِنْ شَاءَ اللَّهُ}} “God willing”.

ex.tr: If you need anything, call me.
If you don't understand, ask me.
If I were you, I'd accept.
If I'd known, I'd have told you.

blocks.tip: {{إِذَا}} + past, then whatever you'd normally say: that's most everyday “if” sentences.

mistakes.tr: If you're busy, I'll call later.
mistakes.why: After {{إِذَا}}, use the past form.

mistakes.tr: If you're late, we'll go without you.
mistakes.why: A result starting with {{سَـ}} needs {{فَـ}}.

practice.q: Making plans with a friend. Choose your replies.

lines.tr: Shall we go to the sea tomorrow?

lines.why: After {{فِي}}: -i; the film is an object: -an.

practice.q: Tell a man: “If I were you, I'd accept.”
Your turn: say what you'll do this weekend if the weather is good, and what you'd do if you were rich.

answers.t: إِذَا كَانَ الْجَوُّ جَمِيلًا، فَسَأَمْشِي فِي الْجِبَالِ.
answers.r: idhā kāna l-jawwu jamīlan, fa-sa-amshī fī l-jibāli.
answers.tr: If the weather's nice, I'll walk in the mountains.

answers.t: لَوْ كُنْتُ غَنِيًّا، لَاشْتَرَيْتُ بَيْتًا قُرْبَ الْبَحْرِ.
answers.r: law kuntu ghaniyyan, la-shtaraytu baytan qurba l-baḥri.
answers.tr: If I were rich, I'd buy a house near the sea.
